key_insight: DenseNet121 led ten pretrained models in breast tumor image classification, achieving 99.4% test accuracy and 0.999 AUC-ROC.
clinical_relevance: This diagnostic imaging study—not drug discovery—suggests potential for interpretable breast cancer classification support, but does not establish clinical readiness.
method: Benchmarked ten ImageNet-pretrained models for benign-versus-malignant classification.
Used BreakHis histopathology images with a patient-level split.
Applied Grad-CAM, LIME, Integrated Gradients, and LRP to explain predictions.
evidence_signal: On the BreakHis test set, DenseNet121 significantly outperformed all other models (reported p < 0.001), while explanations highlighted nuclei-rich and glandular regions.
watch_item: External validation and prospective clinical evaluation are not reported in the abstract; explanation maps alone do not establish clinical reliability.
paper_title: Interpretable Deep Learning Models for Breast Cancer Diagnosis Using Medical Imaging
